changes.text: Regime moved from Risk-on (4 of 6) to Mixed (3 of 6): high yield/Treasuries turned defensive; equal-weight/cap-weight S&P 500 turned risk-on; cyclical vs defensive sectors turned defensive.
New divergence: equities versus credit. S&P 500 3-month rupee return +0.9%; high-yield spread +0.59pp over 3 months. Equities rose while credit spreads widened sharply.
The chips-versus-Indian-IT gap flipped from +21.4pp to -33.1pp, a swing of 54 points: semiconductors led in September, Indian IT now.
No longer a persistent leader: Bitcoin.
Cash is now a persistent leader (INR cash): a defensive sign, since it ranks high only when most assets fall.
Breadth narrowed: 4 of 19 assets rose, against 8 in September.
No longer a persistent laggard: UST 20Y+, Nifty 50, Midcap 150.
The rupee turned: it weakened 0.7% in September and strengthened 0.9% this month, so currency went from helping to hurting rupee returns on dollar assets.
Brent topped the quilt again (+14.5% in September, +17.7% now).
Fed net liquidity turned from rising (+0.1%) to falling (-0.6%).

Valuation readings changed: Korea from Average (55th percentile) to Cheap (9th); China large from Cheap (19th percentile) to Below average (23rd); Japan from Expensive (94th percentile) to Average (58th), mostly an earnings-data update.
Cross-asset dispersion rose from 5.4% to 7.1%: winners and losers drifted further apart.
